s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and adnexal mass with associated non-pitting edema of the left leg
salient_findings: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
Multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa on ultrasound
key_facts: 25-year-old nulliparous woman
1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
Regular menses
No tobacco or alcohol use
Afebrile, blood pressure 110/80 mmHg, pulse 88 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Cardiac and respiratory examinations were unremarkable
Neurologic exam was normal
Firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant
Multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa on ultrasound
Normal baseline hematologic, biochemical, thyroid, renal, and HIV/HBV/HCV serologies
Normal tumor markers
Negative Pap smear
Double inferior vena cava identified on CT scan

differentials: Sex cord tumor with annular tubules
per_call: Sex cord tumor with annular tubules

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Concerning imaging findings for an ovarian neoplasm and presence of a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to ovarian cystadenocarcinoma, with a possible mucinous component given the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Another type of ovarian cancer that could explain the patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including the large solid-cystic lesion

shortlist.label: Ovarian teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the patient's age and the presence of a complex mass in the right adnexa, although less likely than the carcinomas

shortlist.label: Granulosa cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: A type of sex cord-stromal tumor that could explain the patient's symptoms, including the presence of a large mass and non-pitting edema

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, solid-cystic lesion in the right adnexa, along with the imaging findings and the concern for an ovarian neoplasm, makes ovarian cystadenocarcinoma a likely diagnosis. The normal tumor markers do not rule out this diagnosis, as some ovarian cancers can have normal markers.

rejected.label: Ovarian teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are typically more common in younger women and often present with more acute symptoms, which does not fit this patient's insidious onset of symptoms.

rejected.label: Granulosa cell tumor
rejected.why: These tumors often present with hormonal symptoms due to estrogen production, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific mention of mucinous features on imaging makes this less likely than ovarian cystadenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous cystadenocarcinoma, the specific type of ovarian cancer is not clearly indicated by the provided information, making ovarian cystadenocarcinoma a broader and more encompassing choice.
